description: Lightroom-rendered JPEG with Develop edits (raw supported). region crops the rendered frame after develop crop/rotation: normalized x/y/width/height, origin top-left, x right, y down. width/height/bytes are actual; requested_size is the edge asked of Lightroom; scaled_by_server is true when the server scaled Lightroom's larger image down. Lightroom sometimes answers that it has no preview pixels for a photo, typically right after a change; the call asks again for about 20 s and, if it still has none, fails with that reason: ask again later. The photo open in Develop gets no thumbnail, since Lightroom's thumbnail there can be stale or an enlarged low-resolution copy: it fails at once, naming render_photo; for that photo take one look before editing and one after, not one per step. Lightroom's preview cache can answer with an enlargement of a smaller cached preview, most often on a cropped photo, without saying so; judge fine sharpness with get_photo_detail. See size for cost/edge rules. Rules: region must fit within the rendered frame (x + width and y + height at most 1).

photo_ids.description: One photo ID or file path

region.description: Rectangle within the rendered preview, including its develop crop and displayed orientation. Pixel bounds round outward. Region calls request a larger source by dividing size by the longest normalized side, capped at 2048; requested_size reports that source request. A source over 2000px is scaled to 2000px before the crop; otherwise its pixels are cut as Lightroom rendered them.

size.description: Longest edge returned: cull is 864, review 1728, sizes Lightroom 16.0 renders itself for 3:2 raws, so they usually arrive without resampling; numeric 64-2048 means exactly that edge; default cull, the frequent call. The server scales a larger Lightroom image down to this edge, at most 2000px, within 3.5 MiB; a smaller image is returned as Lightroom made it. cull is for choosing among frames, review for a whole-frame look at rendering, tone and mask edges. Image tokens grow with pixel area (Claude: about width x height / 750) and repeat each turn in history.
